&#8220;estimate,&#8221; &#8220;expect,&#8221; &#8220;project,&#8221; &#8220;intend,&#8221; &#8220;commit,&#8221; &#8220;believe&#8221; and similar expressions, the Company intends to identify forward-looking statements.&#160;&#160;Such statements are subject to certain risks, uncertainties and assumptions, including those described in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.&#160;&#160;Should one or more of these risks or uncertainties materialize, or should underlying assumptions prove incorrect, actual results may vary materially from those anticipated, estimated, expected, projected, intended, committed or believed.&#160;&#160;Such risks and uncertainties include, but are not limited to, the following factors: (i) general economic conditions, whether national or regional, that could affect the demand for loans and other banking services or lead to increased loan losses; (ii) competitive factors, including increased competition with community, regional and national financial institutions that may lead to pricing pressures on rates the Bank charges on loans and pays on deposits or reduce the value of real estate collateral securing the Bank&#8217;s loans; (iii) loss of customers of greatest value to the Bank or other losses; (iv) increasing or decreasing interest rate environments that could lead to decreased net interest margin and increased volatility of rate sensitive loans and deposits; (v) changing business conditions in the banking industry; (vi) changes in the regulatory environment or new legislation; (vii) changes in technology or required investments in technology; (viii) credit quality deterioration which could cause an increase in the provision for loan losses; (ix) dividend restrictions; (x) continued volatility in Afghanistan, Iran and elsewhere in the Middle East, and its impact on world oil prices and supply; and (xi) fiscal instability in Europe and its potential impact on the U.S. economy.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">PART I</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Item 1.&#160;&#160;Business</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-VARIANT: small-caps; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Business Development</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">The Company</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Mission Community Bancorp (&#8220;Bancorp&#8221; or the Company&#8221;) is a California corporation registered as a bank holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended, and is headquartered in San Luis Obispo, California.&#160;&#160;It was incorporated on September 22, 2000 and acquired all the outstanding shares of Mission Community Bank in a one bank holding company organization effective December 15, 2000.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Bancorp&#8217;s principal activity is the ownership of all of the outstanding common stock of Mission Community Bank (&#8220;the Bank&#8221;) and any other subsidiaries we may acquire or establish.&#160;&#160;Bancorp formed a wholly-owned subsidiary, Mission Community Capital Trust I, in 2003 solely to facilitate the issuance of trust preferred securities.&#160;&#160;In May 2010, Bancorp formed Mission Asset Management, Inc. (&#8220;MAM&#8221;), in order to purchase certain of the non-performing assets of the Bank, which assets were purchased in June 2010.&#160;&#160;On October 21, 2011, Santa Lucia Bank, headquartered in Atascadero, California, (&#8220;Santa Lucia&#8221;) was merged with and into the Bank.&#160;&#160;In conjunction with the Santa Lucia merger, Bancorp acquired all of the common securities of Santa Lucia Bancorp (CA) Capital Trust, the trust preferred subsidiary of Santa Lucia Bancorp (&#8220;SL Bancorp&#8221;), and assumed SL Bancorp&#8217;s junior subordinated debt liabilities to Santa Lucia Bancorp (CA) Capital Trust.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2012 Bancorp and its consolidated subsidiaries (&#8220;the Company&#8221;) had approximately $435 million in total assets and $37 million in shareholders&#8217; equity.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s address is 3380 South Higuera Street, San Luis Obispo, California 9340, and its telephone number is (805) 782-5000.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Bancorp&#8217;s principal source of income is earnings from the Bank, although supplemental sources of income may be explored in the future.&#160;&#160;Its expenditures, including (but not limited to) salaries and benefits for Bancorp&#8217;s officers, the payment of dividends to shareholders, if and when declared by the Board of Directors, the cost of servicing debt, legal fees, audit fees and shareholder costs will generally be paid from dividends paid to us by Mission Community Bank.&#160;&#160;Due to losses realized by Mission Community Bank from 2008 through 2011, the Bank is currently unable to pay dividends to Bancorp without prior regulatory approval.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Part II&#8212;Item 5&#8212;Market for Common Equity, Related Shareholder Matters and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities&#8212;Dividends.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At the present time, we have no plans to engage in any activities other than acting as a bank holding company for the Bank and MAM, and any other banks we may acquire, although in the future we may consider engaging in other activities which are permissible for a bank holding company, provided that engaging in such activities is deemed by the Board of Directors to be in the best interest of Mission Community Bancorp and its shareholders.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Bancorp neither owns nor leases any material property, but instead makes use of the premises, equipment and furniture of the Bank.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Each of Bancorp and the Bank were certified by the U.S. Department of the Treasury as a Community Development Financial Institution (&#8220;CDFI&#8221;) with a commitment to providing financial services to low and moderate-income communities prior to losing that status in 2012.&#160;&#160;In order to maintain its CDFI status, any bank holding company which owns more than 25% of the voting shares or otherwise controls a company or a bank with CDFI status must itself be a CDFI.&#160;&#160;Neither the Bancorp nor the Bank retains its CDFI status due to a change in control in the second quarter of 2010 pursuant to which the ownership by our principal shareholder, which is not a CDFI, increased from 24.7% of our common stock to more than 75% of our common stock.&#160;&#160;Nonetheless, in addition to pursuing our general commercial banking business, we intend to continue our commitment to providing financial services to low and moderate-income communities.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Pursuant to the terms of our Series A and Series C preferred stock, which shares were issued to the Community Development Financial Institutions Fund of the U.S. Department of the Treasury (&#8220;the CDFI Fund&#8221;) in conjunction with funding relating to our previous CDFI status, the CDFI Fund has the right to cause us to redeem all of the Series A and Series C preferred stock, given the loss of our CDFI status.&#160;&#160;Therefore, we are expecting the CDFI Fund to exercise its right to cause us to redeem our Series A and Series C preferred stock in 2013 for an aggregate of approximately $1.0 million.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Further, in conjunction with funding relating to our CDFI status, 20,500 shares of non-voting Series B preferred stock were issued to the National Community Investment Fund in 2001. With the loss of our CDFI status, we were requested in 2012 to redeem the Series B preferred stock and the redemption was accomplished at a 30% discount, for an aggregate of $143,500 with the Company recognizing a gain of $61,500.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Mission Community Bank</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Bancorp, is a California state-chartered bank headquartered in San Luis Obispo, California.&#160;&#160;It is also a member of the Federal Reserve System.&#160;&#160;Its deposits are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) up to the applicable limits of the law.&#160;&#160;Mission Community Bank opened for business on December 18, 1997, and currently operates five full service locations along the Central Coast of California: in the cities of San Luis Obispo, Paso Robles, Atascadero and Arroyo Grande&#160;&#160;in San Luis Obispo County, and in Santa Maria&#160;&#160;in northern Santa Barbara County.&#160;&#160;We also operate a Business Banking Center in San Luis Obispo, which is primarily engaged in originating and servicing SBA-guaranteed loans, and a Food and Agribusiness Loan Production Office in Oxnard, California.&#160;&#160;Our administrative offices are also located in San Luis Obispo.&#160;&#160;Our primary market area is San Luis Obispo County, northern Santa Barbara County and portions of Ventura County.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank is a community bank engaged in the general commercial banking business along the Central Coast of California. It offers a variety of deposit and loan products to individuals, businesses and non-profit organizations<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.</font> At December 31, 2012, the Bank, on a stand-alone basis, had approximately $433 million in assets, $244 million in loans, $389 million in deposits, and $41 million in shareholders&#8217; equity.&#160;&#160;The Santa Lucia merger in October 2011 increased the Bank&#8217;s total assets and total deposits by approximately $220 million at that time.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Mission Asset Management, Inc. (&#8220;MAM&#8221;)</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Mission Asset Management, Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Bancorp, was established in June 2010 to facilitate the orderly sale or resolution of the Bank&#8217;s foreclosed real estate and certain lower-quality loans.&#160;&#160;MAM purchases assets from the Bank at their &#8220;fair value.&#8221;&#160;&#160;If the sale or other resolution of an asset within the first the 90 days of MAM&#8217;s ownership results in a gain, that gain will be given to the Bank.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2010 the Bank reclassified $22.4 million of problem loans (including $10.3 million of nonaccrual loans) to &#8220;held for sale,&#8221; writing down the value of those loans to $16.9 million through charge-offs to the allowance for loan and lease losses.&#160;&#160;Those loans, along with $1.0 million of other real estate owned (&#8220;OREO&#8221;), were sold from the Bank to MAM at the aggregate purchase price of $17.9 million.&#160;&#160;During 2011 MAM&#8217;s loan portfolio was reduced by $15.1 million to $3.6 million, through loan payments and payoffs, loan participations and foreclosures.&#160;&#160;Net OREO held by MAM increased from $2.6 million to $3.1 million during 2011, although $2.8 million was received from the sale of OREO during 2011.&#160;&#160;During 2012 MAM&#8217;s loan portfolio was reduced from $3.6 million to $1.4 million, through loan payments and payoffs, even though an additional $4.6 million of loans were sold by the Bank to MAM during the year.&#160;&#160;OREO held by MAM was reduced from $3.1 million to $0.5 million during 2012 from the sale of properties, despite the fact that an additional $1.2 million of OREO was sold by the Bank to MAM in 2012.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-VARIANT: small-caps; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Business of Issuer</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management and the Board of Directors evaluate and manage the operations and financial performance on a Company-wide basis.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, all financial services operations are considered by management to be a single operating segment.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Principal Products, Services, and Markets</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other than holding the shares of the Bank, Bancorp conducts no significant activities. Bancorp is authorized, with the prior approval of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the &#8220;Federal Reserve Board&#8221;), its principal regulator, to engage in a variety of activities which are deemed closely related to the business of banking.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank offers checking and savings accounts, money market accounts and time certificates of deposit.&#160;&#160;On the loan side, the Bank offers commercial, agribusiness, government guaranteed, real estate, automobile and other installment and term loans and leases and provides other customary banking services. Although the Bank does not operate a trust department or provide international services, it makes trust services and international services available through correspondent institutions.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The areas in which the Company has directed virtually all of its lending activities are commercial loans (including government-guaranteed, agricultural and municipal loans),&#160;&#160;real estate loans, construction loans, consumer loans and lease financing.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2012, these five categories of loans accounted for approximately 20.5%, 73.8%, 4.9%, 0.4%, and 0.4% respectively, of the Company&#8217;s gross loan portfolio.&#160;&#160;As of that date, $192.9 million, or 78.7%, of the Company&#8217;s loans consisted of real estate loans, for commercial development or for single family residences&#160;&#160;and interim construction loans.&#160;&#160;This represents a $5.8 million increase in real estate and construction loans from the prior year&#8217;s combined total of $187.1 million.&#160;&#160;In percentage terms, real estate and construction loans decreased from 80.0% to 78.7% of the loan portfolio.&#160;&#160;Under the regulatory definition of commercial real estate&#8212;which excludes owner-occupied properties&#8212;the Company&#8217;s commercial real estate concentration was reduced to $85.8 million, or 35.0% of gross loans.&#160;&#160;See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Loan Concentrations</font> in Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis under Item 7 of Part II of this report.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2012, the Bank, on a stand-alone basis, had 16,201 deposit accounts, including 11,608 demand accounts (both non-interest-bearing and interest-bearing, including NOW and money market deposit accounts) totaling $229.6 million; 3,159 savings accounts with balances totaling $55.3 million; and 1,434 time certificates of deposit totaling $102.5 million.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The principal sources of the Bank&#8217;s revenues are interest and fees on loans, interest on investments including federal funds sold and deposits in other banks, gains from sale of loans, service charges on deposit accounts and, occasionally, gain on securities sales, grants and awards.&#160;&#160;Also, for 2011 the Company recognized a substantial portion of non-interest income from changes in the fair value of warrant liabilities.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Distribution Methods of the Products and Services</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank&#8217;s primary service area consists of San Luis Obispo County and northern Santa Barbara County and portions of Ventura County, which lie centrally within the State of California along the Pacific Ocean.&#160;&#160;Secondary market areas include cities and unincorporated areas in the neighboring counties, including Monterey, Kern, Kings, Fresno, and south Santa Barbara Counties.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank operates out of five full service offices (in the cities of San Luis Obispo, Paso Robles, Atascadero, Arroyo Grande and Santa Maria) plus an administrative and loan production facility, which is located in the city of San Luis Obispo.&#160;&#160;In the first quarter of 2011, the Bank opened a loan production office for food and agribusiness lending in Oxnard, California.&#160;&#160;The Bank provides some financial services through direct contact by calling officers who call on clients in the neighboring counties.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Most of the Bank&#8217;s customers are small- to medium-sized businesses and their owners, retail customers, and&#160;&#160;farmers.&#160;&#160;Most of the Bank&#8217;s deposit customers are attracted to the Bank by relationship banking, the Bank&#8217;s involvement and support in local community activities, and advertising.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The business plan of the Bank emphasizes the delivery of highly specialized financial services in a professional and personalized manner to individuals and businesses in its service area.&#160;&#160;Its key strengths are customer service, the products and value we offer our customers and an experienced management team who understand and appreciate the communities and customer needs of those we serve.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank serves its customers through Internet technology by making available a &#8220;remote capture&#8221; deposit product, as well as enhanced Internet Banking, electronic Bill-Pay and ACH origination.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank participates in the Certificate of Deposit Account Registry Service (&#8220;CDARS&#8221;) program.&#160;&#160;This program permits the Bank&#8217;s customers to place all of their certificates of deposit at the Bank and have those deposits fully-insured by the FDIC.&#160;&#160;The CDARS program acts as a clearinghouse, matching deposits from one institution in the CDARS network of approximately 3,000 banks with other network banks (in increments of less than the $250 thousand FDIC insurance limit), so funds that a customer places with the Bank essentially remain on the Bank&#8217;s balance sheet.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Status of any Publicly Announced New Products or Services</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2012 the Bank received a $415 thousand Bank Enterprise Award through the U.S. Department of the Treasury&#8217;s Community Development Financial Institution Program, based on lending activity in 2011.&#160;&#160;In 2011 the Bank received $500 thousand from the BEA program.&#160;&#160;These grants were recognized in non-interest income.&#160;&#160;Since 2001 the Bank has received BEA grants totaling $4.3 million, including those received in 2011 and 2012.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Competition</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank operates in a highly competitive market that is served by local and regional community banks,&#160;&#160;large money center banks, credit unions, and investment brokerage businesses.&#160;&#160;Mission Community Bank offers its customers the advantages of dealing with a locally owned and dedicated community bank, with local decision making, that supports local activities, lends to local businesses and consumers and provides local employment opportunities.&#160;&#160;Larger banks may have a competitive advantage because of higher lending limits and major advertising and marketing campaigns in addition to a broader line of financial products and services that the Bank does not offer.&#160;&#160;To better compete and serve its customers, the Bank has made arrangements with other financial service providers to extend such services to its customers where possible.&#160;&#160;For borrowers requiring loans in excess of the Bank&#8217;s legal lending limits, the Bank sells loan participations to other independent banks, retaining the portion of such loans that is within its legal lending limits, and purchases participations from them under similar circumstances.&#160;&#160;Commercial banks compete with savings and loan associations, credit unions, other financial institutions, securities brokerage firms, and other entities for funds.&#160;&#160;For instance, yields on corporate and government debt securities and other commercial paper may affect the ability of commercial banks to attract and hold deposits.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank utilizes technology to improve its competitive advantages through use of ATMs, Internet Banking, ACH origination, electronic bill pay, email, remote deposit capture and credit card and merchant card relationships.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">To compete effectively, the Bank has created a sales and service culture that combines the experience of its senior officers with the focus on the individual needs of its customers that is found at the best community banks.&#160;&#160;The Bank also relies on local advertising programs, direct personal contact by its officers, directors, employees and shareholders and specialized services such as courier pick-up and remote deposit capture.&#160;&#160;The Bank believes it provides a level of service and decision-making responsiveness not generally offered by larger institutions.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;As in most U.S. cities, large banks compete in our service area.&#160;&#160;However, community banks are more prominent in our market.&#160;&#160;As such, we believe our primary competitors for individuals and small- and medium-sized business customers are the community banks, which can provide the service and responsiveness that is attractive to these customer segments.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Within San Luis Obispo County and northern Santa Barbara County, and based on data from the FDIC as of June 30, 2012, there were 16 banks with 100 branches with aggregate deposits of $6.3 billion.&#160;&#160;The Bank&#8217;s deposits represent a 6.3% share of this market.&#160;&#160;Of the 16 banks, five were community banks with less than $1 billion in assets.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Dependence on One or a Few Major Customers</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank is limited, due to legal lending limits, in the size of loans it can make to any one borrower or group of affiliates.&#160;&#160;It has in its portfolio approximately 800 loans to approximately 625 loan customers.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2012, the Bank&#8217;s legal lending limit to a single borrower and its affiliates was approximately $11.4 million on a secured basis, and was $6.8 million for unsecured loans, based on the level of shareholder&#8217;s equity plus reserves of approximately $45.6 million.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank has a higher than average dependence (as measured by peer group analysis) on larger deposit balances (deposits of $100,000 or more) with a total of 984 deposit accounts holding $273.9 million in deposits as of December 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;Included in those totals are 29 customers with deposits of $1 million or more, totaling $77.6 million, with one local customer relationship representing approximately 7% of the Bank&#8217;s total deposits as of December 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;Management works with large depositors to &#8220;ladder out,&#8221; or spread, certificate of deposit maturities over time in order to both minimize liquidity risk for the Bank and to provide a better return for the customer on their deposited funds.&#160;&#160;These large deposit balances have been reasonably stable during the past several years and are consistent with the Bank&#8217;s deposit and funding strategy.&#160;&#160;Also included in the totals above are 76 non-interest-bearing transaction accounts, of which $46.4 million exceeds the normal FDIC insurance limit, but which had been subject to unlimited FDIC insurance coverage until December 31, 2012, under the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>The Bank has a contingency funding plan in place to address any potential loss of these large deposits.&#160;&#160;This plan includes potential secured borrowings from the Federal Home Loan Bank of San Francisco (&#8220;FHLB&#8221;), the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, and potential unsecured borrowings from a correspondent bank.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">To date, the Bank&#8217;s business has not been materially seasonal in nature.&#160;&#160;However, a limited amount of seasonality is developing with the growth of our agricultural lending portfolio.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Recent Developments</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On October 21, 2011, the two mergers contemplated under the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated June 24, 2011 by and among the Company, Carpenter Fund Manager GP, LLC (&#8220;Carpenter&#8221;), as General Partner of Carpenter Community BancFund L.P. and Carpenter Community BancFund-A., L.P. (the &#8220;Funds&#8221;), Mission Community Bank, SL Bancorp and Santa Lucia Bank (&#8220;SL Bank&#8221;) (the &#8220;Merger Agreement&#8221;) were consummated.&#160;&#160;The Funds are the principal shareholders of the Company and Carpenter is the general partner of the Funds.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;Subject to the terms and conditions of the Merger Agreement, SL Bancorp was merged with CCI One Acquisition Corporation, a newly-formed wholly-owned subsidiary of the Funds (&#8220;CCI One&#8221;), with SL Bancorp being the surviving corporation (the &#8220;Merger&#8221;).&#160;&#160;At the effective time of the Merger, each outstanding share of SL Bancorp common stock, other than any shares dissenting from the Merger, was converted into the right to receive $0.35 in cash or an aggregate of approximately $700,000 (the &#8220;Merger Consideration&#8221;).&#160;&#160;In addition, immediately prior to the Merger CCI One purchased from the United States Department of the Treasury, for an aggregate purchase price of $2.8 million, the outstanding preferred stock and warrants issued by SL Bancorp in the Troubled Asset Relief Program. Immediately following the Merger, Santa Lucia Bank, the wholly-owned subsidiary of SL Bancorp, was merged with and into Mission Community Bank, with Mission Community Bank being the surviving bank (the &#8220;Bank Merger&#8221;).&#160;&#160;See Note U to the consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Also on October&#160;21, 2011, the Company entered into a First Supplemental Indenture with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as trustee.&#160; Pursuant to the First Supplemental Indenture, the Company has assumed the obligations of SL Bancorp under that certain Indenture dated as of April&#160;28, 2006 by and between SL Bancorp and Wells Fargo, National Association, as trustee (the &#8220;Indenture&#8221;)(the &#8220;Debt Assumption&#8221;).&#160; Pursuant to the Indenture an aggregate of $5,155,000 in Junior Subordinated Debt Securities due July&#160;7, 2036 (the &#8220;Debt Securities&#8221;) were issued by SL Bancorp.&#160; The Debt Assumption was undertaken in connection with the merger transactions described above.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;The Debt Securities were issued in connection with a private placement completed on April&#160;28, 2006 of $5,155,000 of trust preferred securities (the &#8220;TruPS Securities&#8221;) issued through Santa Lucia Bancorp (CA) Statutory Trust (the &#8220;Trust&#8221;).&#160; In connection with this issuance, SL Bancorp entered into an Amended and Restated Trust Agreement, dated April&#160;28, 2006, among SL Bancorp, Wells Fargo Bank, National Association and the administrators named therein, pursuant to which the TruPS Securities were issued.&#160; The Securities require quarterly distributions and bear interest at a variable rate which resets quarterly at the three-month LIBOR rate plus 1.48% per annum.&#160; The TruPS Securities mature 30 years from issuance and are redeemable, in whole or in part, without penalty.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Effect of Government Policies and Regulations</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Banking is a business that depends on interest rate differentials.&#160;&#160;In general, the difference between the interest rate paid by the Bank on its deposits and other borrowings and the interest rate received by the Bank on loans extended to its customers and securities held in the Bank&#8217;s portfolio comprise the major portion of the Bank&#8217;s earnings.&#160;&#160;These rates are highly sensitive to many factors that are beyond the control of the Bank. Accordingly, the earnings and growth of the Bank are subject to the influence of domestic and foreign economic conditions, including inflation, recessions and unemployment.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The commercial banking business is not only affected by general economic conditions but is also influenced by the monetary and fiscal policies of the federal government and the policies of regulatory agencies, particularly the Federal Reserve Board (&#8220;FRB&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The FRB implements national monetary policies (with objectives such as curbing inflation, combating recession and reducing unemployment) by its open-market operations in U.S. Government securities, by adjusting the required level of reserves for financial institutions subject to its reserve requirements and by varying the discount rates applicable to borrowings by depository institutions.&#160;&#160;The actions of the Federal Reserve Board in these areas influence the growth of bank loans, investments and deposits and also affect interest rates charged on loans and paid on deposits.&#160;&#160;Except to the extent that the FRB issues statements indicating its planned courses of action, the nature and impact of any future changes in monetary policies cannot be predicted.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">From time to time, legislation is enacted which has the effect of increasing the cost of doing business, limiting or expanding permissible activities or affecting the competitive balance between banks and other financial institutions.&#160;&#160;Proposals to change the laws and regulations governing the operations and taxation of banks, bank holding companies and other financial institutions are frequently made in Congress, in the California legislature and before various bank regulatory agencies and other professional agencies.&#160;&#160;For example, the Bank&#8217;s ability to originate and sell SBA loans would be severely impacted if federal appropriations for the SBA lending program were curtailed or eliminated.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Supervision and Regulation</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Both federal and state laws extensively regulate banks and bank holding companies.&#160;&#160;This regulation is intended primarily for the protection of depositors and the Deposit Insurance Fund and not for the benefit of shareholders of the Company.&#160;&#160;The following is a summary of particular statutes, regulations and regulatory guidance affecting the Company and the Bank.&#160;&#160;This summary is not intended to be a complete explanation of such statutes, regulations or guidance, all of which are subject to change in the future, nor does it fully address their effects and potential effects on the Company and the Bank.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulation of Mission Community Bancorp&#8212;General</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Mission Community Bancorp is a registered bank holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended, and is regulated by the Federal Reserve Board.&#160;&#160;The Company is required to file periodic reports with the Federal Reserve Board and such additional information as the Federal Reserve Board may require pursuant to the Bank Holding Company Act.&#160;&#160;The Federal Reserve Board may conduct examinations of the Company and its subsidiaries, which includes the Bank.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank Holding Company Act requires every bank holding company to obtain the prior approval of the Federal Reserve Board before acquiring substantially all the assets of any bank or bank holding company or ownership or control of any voting shares of any bank or bank holding company, if, after the acquisition, it would own or control, directly or indirectly, more than 5% of the voting shares of the bank or bank holding company.&#160;&#160;The principal exceptions to these prohibitions involve non-bank activities identified by statute, by Federal Reserve regulation, or by Federal Reserve order as activities so closely related to the business of banking or of managing or controlling banks as to be a proper incident thereto, including securities brokerage services, investment advisory services, fiduciary services, and management advisory and data processing services, among others. A bank holding company that also qualifies as and elects to become a &#8220;financial holding company&#8221; may engage in a broader range of activities that are financial in nature (and complementary to such activities), specifically non-bank activities identified as financial in nature or incidental to a financial activity by the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act of 1999 or by Federal Reserve and Treasury regulation.&#160;&#160;Activities that are defined as financial in nature include securities underwriting, dealing, and market making, sponsoring mutual funds and investment companies, engaging in insurance underwriting and agency activities, and making merchant banking investments in non-financial companies. To become and remain a financial holding company, a bank holding company and its subsidiary banks must be well capitalized, well managed, and, except in limited circumstances, have at least a satisfactory rating under the Community Reinvestment Act.&#160;&#160;The Company has no current intention of becoming a financial holding company, but may do so at some point in the future if deemed appropriate in view of opportunities or circumstances at the time.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company and the Bank are deemed to be affiliates of each other within the meaning set forth in the Federal Reserve Act and are subject to Sections 23A and 23B of the Federal Reserve Act. The Federal Reserve Board has also issued Regulation W, which codifies prior regulations under Sections 23A and 23B of the Federal Reserve Act and interpretative guidance with respect to affiliate transactions.&#160;&#160;This means, for example, that there are limitations on loans by the Bank to affiliates, and that all affiliate transactions must satisfy certain limitations and otherwise be on terms and conditions at least as favorable to the Bank as would be available for non-affiliates. In addition, we must comply with the Federal Reserve Act and Regulation O issued by the Federal Reserve Board, which require that loans and extensions of credit to our executive officers, directors and principal shareholders, or any company controlled by any such persons, shall, among other conditions, be made on substantially the same terms and follow credit-underwriting procedures no less stringent than those prevailing at the time for comparable transactions with non-insiders.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Regulations and policies of the Federal Reserve Board require a bank holding company to serve as a source of financial and managerial strength to its subsidiary banks.&#160;&#160;It is the Federal Reserve Board&#8217;s policy that a bank holding company should stand ready to use available resources to provide adequate capital funds to a subsidiary bank during periods of financial stress or adversity and should maintain the financial flexibility and capital-raising capacity to obtain additional resources for assisting a subsidiary bank.&#160;&#160;Under certain conditions, the Federal Reserve Board may conclude that certain actions of a bank holding company, such as a payment of a cash dividend, would constitute an unsafe and unsound banking practice.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Federal Reserve Board also has the authority to regulate bank holding companies&#8217; debt, including the authority to impose interest rate ceilings and reserve requirements on such debt. Under certain circumstances, the Federal Reserve Board may require a bank holding company to file written notice and obtain its approval prior to purchasing or redeeming its equity securities, unless certain conditions are met.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The securities of the Company are also subject to the requirements of the Securities Act, and matters related thereto are regulated by the Securities and Exchange Commission.&#160;&#160;Certain issuances may also be subject to the California corporate securities law as administered by the California Commissioner of Corporations.&#160;&#160;The Company is subject to the public reporting requirements of the Securities and Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, generally applicable to publicly held companies, under Section 15(d) of the Exchange Act.&#160;&#160;Companies which file a registration statement under the Securities Act are required under Section 15(d) of the Exchange Act for at least a 12-month period after the effectiveness of such registration statement to file periodic quarterly and annual reports under the Securities Act.&#160;&#160;If and when the Company has more than 2,000 shareholders of record, it will be required to register its securities with the Securities and Exchange Commission under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act at which time its filing of periodic reports, as well as certain other reporting obligations, will become mandatory.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulation of Mission Community Bank&#8212;Generally</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As a California state-chartered bank, the Bank is subject to regulation, supervision and examination by the California Department of Financial Institutions.&#160;&#160;It is also a member of the Federal Reserve System and, as such, is subject to applicable provisions of the Federal Reserve Act and the related regulations promulgated by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.&#160;&#160;In addition, the deposits of the Bank are currently insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) to a maximum of $250,000 per depositor, and potentially higher limits with respect to certain retirement accounts.&#160;&#160;For deposit insurance protection, the Bank pays a quarterly assessment, and occasional mandated special assessments, to the FDIC and is subject to the rules and regulations of the FDIC pertaining to deposit insurance and other matters.&#160;&#160;The regulations of those agencies govern most aspects of the Bank&#8217;s business, including the making of periodic reports by the Bank, and the Bank&#8217;s activities relating to dividends, investments, loans, borrowings, capital requirements, certain check-clearing activities, branching, mergers and acquisitions, reserves against deposits, the issuance of securities and numerous other areas.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The earnings and growth of the Bank is largely dependent on its ability to maintain a favorable differential or &#8220;spread&#8221; between the yield on its interest-earning assets and the rate paid on its deposits and other interest-bearing liabilities.&#160;&#160;As a result, the Bank&#8217;s performance is influenced by general economic condi&#173;tions, both domestic and foreign, the monetary and fiscal policies of the federal government, and the policies of the regulatory agencies, particularly the Federal Reserve Board (see &#8220;Part I&#8212;Item 1&#8212;Business&#8212;Effect of Government Policies and Regulations&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The nature and impact of any future changes in monetary policies cannot be predicted.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Capital Adequacy Requirements</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company and the Bank are subject to the regulations of the Federal Reserve Board governing capital adequacy.&#160;&#160;Those regulations incorporate both risk-based and leverage capital requirements.&#160;&#160;Under existing regulations, the capital requirements for a bank holding company whose consolidated assets are less than $500 million, like the Company, are deemed to be the same as that of its subsidiary bank.&#160;&#160;The Federal Reserve Board has established risk-based and leverage capital guidelines for the banks it regulates, which set total capital requirements and define capital in terms of &#8220;core capital elements,&#8221; or Tier 1 capital, and &#8220;supplemental capital elements,&#8221; or Tier 2 capital.&#160;&#160;Tier 1 capital is generally defined as the sum of the core capital elements less goodwill and certain intangibles.&#160;&#160;The following items are defined as core capital elements: (i) common stockholders&#8217; equity; (ii) qualifying non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock and related surplus; (iii) minority interests in the equity accounts of consolidated subsidiaries; and (iv)&#160;qualifying trust preferred securities up to 25% of core capital elements, net of goodwill, less any associated deferred tax asset.&#160;&#160;As of December&#160;31, 2012, trust preferred securities comprised approximately 13% of the Company's Tier 1 Capital.&#160;&#160;Supplementary capital elements include: (i) allowance for loan and lease losses (but not more than 1.25% of an institution&#8217;s risk-weighted assets); (ii) perpetual preferred stock and related surplus not qualifying as core capital; (iii) hybrid capital instruments, perpetual debt and mandatory convertible debt instruments; and (iv) term subordinated debt and intermediate-term preferred stock and related surplus.&#160;&#160;The maximum amount of supplemental capital elements which qualifies as Tier 2 capital is limited to 100% of Tier 1 capital, net of goodwill.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">-11-</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank is required to maintain a minimum ratio of qualifying total capital to total risk-weighted assets of 8.0% (&#8220;Total Risk-Based Capital Ratio&#8221;), at least one-half of which must be in the form of Tier 1 capital (&#8220;Tier 1 Risk-Based Capital Ratio&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Risk-based capital ratios are calculated to provide a measure of capital that reflects the degree of risk associated with a banking organization&#8217;s operations for both transactions reported on the balance sheet as assets, and transactions, such as letters of credit and recourse arrangements, which are recorded as off-balance sheet items.&#160;&#160;Under the risk-based capital guidelines, the nominal dollar amounts of assets and credit-equivalent amounts of off-balance-sheet items are multiplied by one of several risk adjustment percentages, which range from 0% for assets with very low credit risk, such as certain U.&#160;S. Treasury securities, to 100% for assets with relatively high credit risk, such as business loans.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2012 and December 31, 2011, the Bank&#8217;s Total Risk-Based Capital Ratio was 13.65% and 13.25%, respectively, and its Tier 1 Risk-Based Capital Ratio was 12.40% and 12.00%, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The risk-based capital standards also take into account concentrations of credit and the risks of &#8220;non-traditional&#8221; activities (those that have not customarily been part of the banking business). The regulations require institutions with high or inordinate levels of risk to operate with higher minimum capital standards, and authorize the regulators to review an institution&#8217;s management of such risks in assessing an institution&#8217;s capital adequacy.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Additionally, the regulatory statements of policy on risk-based capital include exposure to interest rate risk as a factor that the regulators will consider in evaluating a bank&#8217;s capital adequacy, although interest rate risk does not impact the calculation of a bank&#8217;s risk-based capital ratios.&#160;&#160;Interest rate risk is the exposure of a bank&#8217;s current and future earnings and equity capital arising from adverse movements in interest rates.&#160;&#160;While interest risk is inherent in a bank&#8217;s role as financial intermediary, it introduces volatility to bank earnings and to the economic value of the bank or bank holding company.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Banks are also required to maintain a leverage capital ratio designed to supplement the risk-based capital guidelines.&#160;&#160;Banks that have received the highest rating of the five categories used by regulators to rate banks and are not anticipating or experiencing any significant growth must maintain a ratio of Tier 1 capital (net of all intangibles) to adjusted total assets (&#8220;Leverage Capital Ratio&#8221;) of at least 3%.&#160;&#160;All other institutions are required to maintain a leverage ratio of at least 100 to 200 basis points above the 3% minimum, for a minimum of 4% to 5%.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to federal regulations, banks must maintain capital levels commensurate with the level of risk to which they are exposed, including the volume and severity of problem loans, and federal regulators may set higher capital requirements when a bank&#8217;s particular circumstances warrant.&#160;&#160;&#160;The Bank&#8217;s Leverage Capital Ratio was 8.61% as of December 31, 2012 and 8.19% at December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;See also Note P to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information regarding regulatory capital.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In December 2010, the Basel Committee on Bank Supervision, a committee of central banks and bank supervisors/regulators from the major industrialized countries that develops broad policy guidelines, which each country&#8217;s supervisors can use to determine the supervisory policies they apply to their home jurisdiction, released its final framework for strengthening international capital and liquidity regulation, identified as &#8220;Basel III.&#8221;&#160;&#160;The FRB announced in December 2011 that it would implement substantially all of the Basel III rules and subsequently proposed new rules to implement the provisions of Basel III.&#160;&#160;The comment period on these rules closed on October 22, 2012.&#160;&#160;If and when fully implemented by the U.S. banking agencies, it would require bank holding companies and their bank subsidiaries to maintain substantially more capital than currently required, with a greater emphasis on common equity.&#160;&#160;The Basel III capital framework, among other things:</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25;">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </font></div>
</td>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Would introduce as a new capital measure, Common Equity Tier 1 (&#8220;CET1&#8221;), more commonly known in the United States as &#8220;Tier 1 Common,&#8221; and would define CET1 narrowly by requiring that most adjustments to regulatory capital measures be made to CET1 and not to the other components of capital, and would expand the scope of the adjustments as compared to existing regulations;</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25;">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </font></div>
</td>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Would require banks to maintain: (i) a newly adopted international standard, a minimum ratio of CET1 to risk-weighted assets of at least 4.5%, plus a 2.5% &#8220;capital conservation buffer&#8221; (which is added to the 4.5% CET1 ratio as that buffer is phased in, effectively resulting in a minimum ratio of CET1 to risk-weighted assets of at least 7%); (ii) an additional &#8220;SIFI buffer&#8221; for those large institutions deemed to be systemically important, ranging from 1.0% to 2.5%, and up to 3.5% under certain conditions; (iii) a minimum ratio of Tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets of at least 6.0%, plus the capital conservation buffer (which is added to the 6.0% Tier 1 capital ratio as that buffer is phased in, effectively resulting in a minimum Tier 1 capital ratio of 8.5% upon full implementation); (iv) a minimum ratio of Total (that is, Tier 1 plus Tier 2) capital to risk-weighted assets of at least 8.0%, plus the capital conservation buffer (which is added to the 8.0% total capital ratio as that buffer is phased in, effectively resulting in a minimum total capital ratio of 10.5% upon full implementation); and (v) as a newly adopted international standard, a minimum leverage ratio of 3%, calculated as the ratio of Tier 1 capital to balance sheet exposures plus certain off-balance sheet exposures (as the average for each quarter of the month-end ratios for the quarter); and</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
